blocks.x: The governed data estate every intelligence program silently depends on. Achala Forge is the platform layer behind it — deployed under NDA, documented for the audit.

Achala Forge operationalizes the lakehouse: medallion pipelines with data contracts, Unity Catalog-class governance, lineage and freshness SLAs, streaming and batch in one estate, and the AI-ready layer (feature stores, vector search, retrieval services) built on the same governed data. It is the substrate domain made product. Forge is deliberately boring where it matters: schema contracts enforced at boundaries, expectations tested on every pipeline, cost telemetry per workload, and audit exports regulators can read. Teams inherit reliability as a measured property — and GenAI programs inherit a corpus that doesn't rot.

Forge is a quantum-inspired optimization core wrapped around the lakehouse. Workloads are compiled into tensor-manifold representations, where tensor contraction and amplitude amplification collapse dimensionality without destroying the interrelations that matter. Scheduling runs at logarithmic complexity, so plan quality holds as the estate grows. Every plan is verified by abstract interpretation and temporal logic before a row moves — deterministic correctness, not best effort. An energy-aware orchestration layer keeps the same plan honest on cost: execution graphs are compressed with low-rank approximation, task profiles decomposed by wavelets, and power thresholds predicted from historical failure patterns.
